hero.micro: First project per company — free. No commitments.

steps.title: From PDF to estimate — three steps

items.d: Floor plans, wall elevations, room schedules — vector PDFs work best; check scanned ones more carefully. No CAD needed.
The app asks a few questions about the project and shows, beside every number, the place on the drawing it came from.
Excel with live formulas, or a Lithuanian-format PDF with the 21% VAT line.

reads.title: What Pathon reads from your drawings
reads.note: Every number carries its unit and a link to the exact spot on the drawing it came from.

trust.sub: Every quantity shows where it came from: read straight off the drawing, computed from an assumption, or a default. Before you quote, the app asks a few questions and shows, beside every number, the place on the drawing it came from.

cards.d: The value comes straight from the room schedule or the plan geometry. Sources cross-checked.
E.g. the ceiling height came from a section, not the room table. The assumption is visible and editable.
Nothing found in the drawing, so a standard value was used. Check it before you quote.

trust.panelFoot: Review the other 43 lines against the drawing.

recalc.title: Change an assumption — quantities follow

assumptions.intro: Every change here recalculates the quantities immediately — wall paint, skim, reveals, skirting, tiling and the rest. There is no “Save” button.
assumptions.demoReadonly: This is a sample project, for viewing only. These are the settings the calculations rest on. Upload your own drawing and you can change them, with the quantities recalculating live.
assumptions.windowsNotFound: No windows found in the drawings
assumptions.windowsNotFoundDesc: Standard suggestions by room type are provided. Check and adjust below.
assumptions.wallThicknessNote: 0.10 m — reveal area and the door openings in the wall area (opening less the painted jambs). LT partitions are typically 0.075–0.10 m, block walls 0.20–0.25 m.
assumptions.puttyLevelNote: A higher level means more skim and more sanding labour.
assumptions.ceilingHeightNote: Directly affects the paintable wall area (perimeter × height) and the drywall ceiling sheet count. If it's one house — use the „All rooms" field below; if heights differ (e.g. attic, garage) — enter per room individually.
assumptions.allRoomsTitle: Enter one height, press Enter — it will be applied to all rooms
assumptions.wallsPaintNote: Some rooms — garage, vestibule — are treated as bare by default. Click to change; the paintable area recalculates live.
assumptions.stretchCeilingNote: Mark the rooms that get a stretch ceiling — their ceiling skimming, priming, painting and sanding drop out of the estimate. Cornice, LED niches and plasterboard ceilings stay.
assumptions.heightRangeErr: Ceiling height must be between {{min}} and {{max}} m.
assumptions.headerTitle: The settings the calculations rest on — skim quality, mixers, wall thickness, height per room
assumptions.introOrphans: A few rows may keep their original values — we will say which ones separately.
assumptions.wallThicknessHint: Partition thickness in metres — used for the reveals row
assumptions.wallThicknessRangeErr: Wall thickness must be between {{min}} and {{max}} m.

questions.readNote_one: Read from the drawing and not waiting for you: {{read}} of {{total}} figures ({{count}} room).
questions.readNote_other: Read from the drawing and not waiting for you: {{read}} of {{total}} figures ({{count}} rooms).
questions.needNumber: Enter a number greater than zero.
questions.openingWidthOdd: {{width}} m is an unusual width for a door. Check the drawing: it may be an opening without a door, a niche or a double door. If it is not a door, correct the width or untick it.
questions.openingsConsequence: An added opening is taken off the painted wall area, shortens the skirting and adds reveals. I will show what it changed in the estimate right away — and you can undo it.
questions.outlineReason: Why I could not find it myself: {{reason}}.
questions.outlineSharedWith: This is room {{su}} — no wall separates it from {{nr}}: one space with an imaginary boundary. I propose the boundary by the table's areas — dashed on the drawing: {{nr}} {{a}} m² (table {{tableA}}), {{su}} {{b}} m² (table {{tableB}}). The wall total does not depend on it.
questions.outlineElsewhere: If the room is larger, click elsewhere inside it on the drawing.
questions.outlineTypeLength: Or without the drawing: type the wall length by hand:
questions.outlineHow: The drawing on the right is waiting for your click. If you miss, I will say so and you can try again.
questions.outlineAllSkipped: You skipped these rooms. Their perimeters are in the question about wall lengths.
questions.splitLoading: Looking for where the boundary could be…
questions.splitByCorner: I propose the boundary through a wall end between these rooms — the dashed line on the drawing. With it both rooms agree with the table.
questions.splitByAreas: I propose the boundary where the rooms divide the way the table states — the dashed line on the drawing.
questions.splitDrawing: Draw the boundary on the drawing: two clicks, wall to wall. “Cancel” brings my proposal back.
questions.splitNoProposal: I could not propose a boundary — draw it yourself: two clicks on the drawing, wall to wall.
questions.skipNote: Skipped means I keep computing with my proposal. You can come back any time.
questions.doneBody: Everything the drawing did not say is answered. Go on to the estimate — or review the rooms one by one to see what I read and where.
questions.doneSkipped: Skipped questions: {{count}} — computed with my proposal. Come back to them any time on the left.
questions.answeredHeight: Answered: ceiling height saved for {{count}} rooms ({{rooms}}).
questions.answeredSplit: Answered: the space is divided — rooms {{rooms}} have their own outlines; the boundary between them is not a wall.
questions.answeredOutline: Answered: room {{rooms}} shown — outline traced along the walls, wall lengths read again.
questions.answeredOutlineAccepted: Answered: room {{rooms}} — the proposed outline accepted, wall lengths read from it.
questions.answeredPerimeterTyped: Answered: room {{rooms}} — wall length typed by hand, {{value}} m.
questions.answeredJoin: Answered: rooms {{rooms}} divided their shared space — each has its own outline, the boundary between them is not a wall.

roomSheet.yourRowsIntro: The drawing does not show these works, but your template has them. Enter a quantity or leave it blank — a blank cell stays blank, nobody writes a zero.
roomSheet.yourRowsNone: All template rows have a quantity.
roomSheet.title: Room check sheet
roomSheet.drawFallback: The drawing file could not be opened — showing its picture.
roomSheet.drawNoOutline: I could not trace this room's outline on the drawing: {{reason}}. Only its number on the plan is marked.
roomSheet.drawNoOutlinePlain: I could not trace this room's outline on the drawing — only its number on the plan is marked.
roomSheet.drawOpenSpace: Open plan with {{rooms}} — no walls separate these rooms, so the shared outline is shown (dashed).
roomSheet.legendWallBorrowed: the plan writes only the equal wall opposite
roomSheet.legendWallOutline: a short piece with no number — from the outline
roomSheet.legendRoomRegion: this room's place on the sheet
roomSheet.legendRoomRegionApprox: this room's approximate place on the sheet
roomSheet.noOutline: This room has no outline on the drawing — only its number's position is shown.
roomSheet.noOpeningMarks: The drawing gives no positions for doors and windows, so none are marked on the plan. The count and sizes are on the card.
roomSheet.cropFailed: The crop could not be shown. Open the drawing.
roomSheet.wholeSheetWhy: I do not know the exact spot on this sheet — showing the whole sheet.
roomSheet.openingsAssumed: Is that the size? Standard sizes — change them if they differ
roomSheet.openingsAddConsequence: An added opening is taken off the painted wall area, shortens the skirting and adds reveals. You can change its size afterwards.
roomSheet.legendOpenings: opening in the wall (door, window or passage)
roomSheet.saveForAll: Save for all {{count}} rooms that ask this
roomSheet.outlinePickFromFact: Show the room on the drawing
roomSheet.outlinePickHint: Click inside room {{room}} — anywhere on its floor.
roomSheet.outlinePickWhy: I will trace the outline along the walls myself and read the wall lengths right away.
roomSheet.outlinePickHintProposal: The proposed outline is dashed on the drawing. If it fits, press Accept on the left; if room {{room}} is larger, click elsewhere inside it.
roomSheet.outlinePickWhyProposal: I will trace the outline along the walls where you click and read the wall lengths at once.
roomSheet.outlineReading: Drawing the outline and reading the wall lengths…
roomSheet.outlineTaken: This place already belongs to room {{room}}. Click inside your room.
roomSheet.outlineOpenWith: The walls here do not separate this room from room {{rooms}} (a space of {{area}} m²) — I cannot draw a separate outline. Enter the perimeter by hand.
roomSheet.outlineOpen: The walls here close {{area}} m² — far more than this room is given. The space looks shared with another room; enter the perimeter by hand.
roomSheet.outlineOutside: There is no space closed by walls here. Click inside the room, not on a wall.
roomSheet.outlineShared: This is room {{rooms}} — no wall separates it from this one. I will propose the boundary on the question screen (the „Klausimai“ button).
roomSheet.outlineNoWalls: I cannot read walls on this sheet. Open the plan that draws the walls and click there.
roomSheet.outlineFailed: The outline could not be drawn. Try another place inside the room.
roomSheet.splitFromFact: Divide the space on the drawing
roomSheet.splitHintFirst: No wall separates this room from room {{rooms}} — you show the boundary. Click by the wall where it starts.
roomSheet.splitHintSecond: Now click by the opposite wall, where the boundary ends. You can see the line on the drawing.
roomSheet.splitHintWhy: No need to be exact: the walls of the two rooms add up to the same total wherever the boundary is — it only divides that total between them.
roomSheet.splitBadLine: This line does not separate the rooms: their numbers must end up on different sides of it. Try again.
roomSheet.splitNotShared: Walls already separate this room from the others — there is nothing to divide.
roomSheet.splitTooMany: More than two rooms share this space — I cannot divide that yet. Enter the perimeters by hand.
roomSheet.wallsConsequence: Not painted: no wall skimming, painting or corners for this room in the estimate.
roomSheet.paskirtisConsequence: The use drives more than the floor — wall and tile rules follow from it too.
roomSheet.floorConsequence: The covering you choose recalculates this room's flooring, skirting and tile skirting. Walls and ceiling stay as they are.
roomSheet.fixSameValue: Saved. The quantities did not change because they were already computed with this very number — it is now confirmed by you instead of assumed.
roomSheet.fixUndone: Fix undone — everything is as it was.
roomSheet.quantitiesEmpty: Nothing from this room reaches the estimate.
roomSheet.quantitiesSummary: These {{facts}} produce {{rows}}. They recalculate on their own when you correct a fact.
roomSheet.noLedger: Quantities for this room are not prepared yet — press “Recalculate”.
roomSheet.overrideShared: This room's share cannot be corrected yet — fix the fact above, or the whole line in the estimate.
roomSheet.overrideSaved: Saved. A recalculation will not overwrite your number.
roomSheet.cornersHighlighted: The corners are marked on the plan on the left.
roomSheet.rippleNone: Recalculated — the quantities did not change.
roomSheet.generalIntro: Not everything comes from the rooms. Check these once for the whole project.
roomSheet.generalCeilingWhy: Ceiling quantities are billed off this number, not off the sum of the rooms.
roomSheet.generalSymbolsWhy: Counted on the plan. Doesn't match? — correct the number here.
roomSheet.generalCeilingPlanTitle: Sum of the areas written on the plan
roomSheet.generalCeilingPlanWhy: The drawing prints no room schedule — ceiling quantities are taken from the room areas written on the plan, not from the sum of the rooms.
roomSheet.generalAuthorIntro: The designer wrote these numbers on the drawing itself. Compare them with ours — we do not take them over, we compute from the drawing.
roomSheet.generalAuthorWhy: Written on the drawing (p. {{page}}). More than a tenth apart? — check which rooms the designer included.
roomSheet.generalAuthorNoOurs: Written on the drawing (p. {{page}}). We do not compute such a row — add it yourself if you need it.
roomSheet.scopeRoomOnNote: The room is in every row. If it is not yours or a duplicate, switch it off: none of its rows will be in the estimate.
roomSheet.scopeRoomOffNote: The room stays on the sheet but is in no row at all — not walls, ceilings, floors or materials.
roomSheet.scopeIntro: How you work on this job. Change one and the quantities recompute at once.

scopeLubosNote.dazomos: Ceiling skimming and painting rows are taken from the schedule area.
scopeLubosNote.ne_musu: No ceiling skimming, priming or painting rows in the estimate. Where a room says otherwise, the room's choice wins.
scopeLubosNote.itempiamos: Stretch ceilings — no skimming or painting; cornice, LED niches and plasterboard stay. Where a room says otherwise, the room's choice wins.

scopeSienosNote.atimti: Door and window openings are deducted from the wall area.
scopeSienosNote.neatimti: Walls are measured straight through the openings — as many finishers do, since cut-outs are waste and labour.

roomSheet.scopeFamiliesNote: Rows of an unticked area will not be in the estimate, along with its materials. Sections belonging to no area always stay.
roomSheet.scopeRoomFamiliesNote: An unticked area leaves this room's rows and their materials. Plumbing and electrics are counted per project — on the general page.

scopeRotbandNote.dalis: Masonry and concrete walls are levelled, plasterboard partitions are not. The drawing does not state wall types, so you set the share; until then a 30 % assumption is used.
scopeRotbandNote.nera: No wall levelling row or Rotband material in the estimate.
scopeRotbandNote.visos: The whole painted wall area is levelled.

roomSheet.unclaimedTitle: Areas written on the plan with no room
roomSheet.unclaimedIntro: These areas are written on the drawing but no room that was read carries them — most likely a room was missed. Add it if it is yours; set its purpose and perimeter on its sheet.
roomSheet.unclaimedWhy: Written on the plan (p. {{page}}), inside no room.
roomSheet.roomAdded: Room {{nr}} added — set its purpose and check the perimeter on its sheet.

scopeKampaiNote.su_vidiniais: Corner length: the room's own corners (corner count × height), the edges of openings (doors, windows) at a standard size, partition junctions and the room perimeter (wall-to-ceiling joint).
scopeKampaiNote.tik_isoriniai: The room's own corners are skimmed without bead. What remains: the edges of openings (doors, windows) at a standard size, partition junctions and the room perimeter (wall-to-ceiling joint).

roomSheet.cropHint: The whole sheet is shown. Zoom in with „+“, by clicking the drawing, or with Ctrl + mouse wheel. „Fit“ brings the whole sheet back. Close with Esc.
roomSheet.cropOutlined: the outlined spot is where the number was read
roomSheet.generalNone: This project has no shared facts.
roomSheet.loadError: The room's data could not be loaded.
roomSheet.noRooms: This project has no rooms yet.
roomSheet.symNoPage: I cannot name the sheet they were counted on.

newProject.errStreamNoResult: The reading stopped without a result. Please try again.
newProject.errNoRooms: No rooms were found in this drawing. Check that you uploaded an interior / floor plan (not a photo, a KŽ table or a facade). If it really is a plan, try again or enter the rooms by hand.
newProject.warnPdfNotDurable: The drawing was not stored durably — exports will work, but the drawing preview may disappear.
newProject.errAborted: Request canceled or timed out. Try a smaller PDF or retry.
newProject.errNetwork: Cannot reach the server. Check your connection.
newProject.errStreamLostButRunning: The connection dropped, but the work continues on the server. The project will appear in “Projektai” in a few minutes — refresh the page. Do not upload again.
newProject.abortedByUser: Canceled. No project was created — you can upload the PDF again.
newProject.cancelledRunContinues: You stopped waiting, but the server had already started reading the drawing and will finish it. If the reading succeeds, the project appears in “Projektai” by itself — there is no need to upload the same PDF again.
newProject.title: New project
newProject.subtitle: The app reads the drawing and prepares the quantities. You check them and enter your prices.
newProject.typeHint: The type decides which quantities are calculated from the drawing.
newProject.otherTypesTitle: Other project types — the interior project fits most finishing work

typeTitles.interior: Reads interior drawings: paintable area, skimming, tiles, skirting
typeTitles.auto: The project type will be determined from the drawing’s contents
typeTitles.kz: Reads an existing bill-of-quantities table out of the PDF

newProject.nameTitle: If left empty, the name is taken from the drawing
newProject.companyTitle: Shown on the exported proposal; can be changed in Settings
newProject.startAnalysisTitle: Read the drawing and prepare the quantities
newProject.startAnalysisHint: It takes about 20 minutes. You can close this window — the work continues on the server and the project appears in your list by itself.
newProject.cancelTitle: Stop waiting in this window. If the drawing is already being read, the server finishes it and the project appears in “Projektai”.
newProject.cancelTitleNoStream: Cancel — no project will be created.
newProject.errStalled: The run stalled (7 min with no answer from the server). Try again — if it keeps happening, tell us.
newProject.errTimeout: The run passed the 45 min limit. Try a smaller PDF or tell us.
newProject.errRunInterrupted: The reading stopped on our server before it finished, so no project was created. Start the reading again.
newProject.errRunFailed: The reading failed, so no project was created. Start the reading again — if it keeps happening, write to us.
newProject.errRunLost: The reading finished, but the result never reached this window, so no project was created. Start the reading again.
newProject.statusRecovering: The connection dropped, but the work continues on the server. Waiting for the result… ({{s}} s) — do not upload again.
newProject.doneNotifBody: Quantities are ready. Come back to review the project.

preflight.disclaimer: A quick guess from the PDF’s text, not a result.
preflight.pickAnotherTitle: Remove this file and upload another
preflight.overrideBlockTitle: Continue knowing that pages past the 100th will not be read

verdict.interior_plan: This looks like an interior design project — the kind we read best.
verdict.table_only: This looks like a bill-of-quantities table rather than a drawing — we probably will not find rooms. Continue anyway?
verdict.photo_or_scan: This PDF is photos or scans with no text. The quantities will still be calculated, but they will need a closer check.
verdict.facade_or_site: These look like facade or site drawings rather than interior plans — we probably will not find rooms. Continue anyway?
verdict.mixed_bundle: This looks like a full technical set — the interior drawings are only part of the file. Every page will be read.
verdict.unknown: We could not tell what kind of drawings these are. It may still work.

q.objectNote: Used in the project name — it does not change any quantity.
q.ceilingLabel: Ceiling height, if you know it
q.ceilingNote: 2.80 m — the usual one. You can leave it empty: heights come from the drawing. Your number waits in settings — one click applies it wherever the drawing gives no height.

lubosNote.dazomos: Ceiling skimming and painting rows come from the schedule area. Any room can be marked otherwise later.
lubosNote.ne_musu: No ceiling skimming, priming or painting rows in the estimate.
lubosNote.itempiamos: Stretch ceilings — no skimming or painting; cornice, LED niches and plasterboard stay.

sienosNote.atimti: Door and window openings are deducted from the wall area.
sienosNote.neatimti: Walls are measured straight through the openings — cut-outs are waste and labour.

q.rememberedNote: As on your last 3 projects — change it if this one is different.
q.familiesAllNote: All ticked. Untick one and its rows will not be in the estimate (nor the materials bought for them).
q.familiesSomeOffNote: Rows from the unticked areas will not be in the estimate, along with their materials. Sections that belong to no area (ventilation, for example) always stay.
